suggestions.issue: Internal self-contradiction about the direction of the method. The definition and plain_english say bottom-up starts at the SOURCE/input and works forward toward the output; but purpose_function (and practical_application's PA example) say it starts at the OUTPUT/lowest physical layer and works UPWARD toward the source. A student cannot tell which way the method actually runs.
suggestions.suggestion: Reconcile the four fields to a single, consistent direction. As written, purpose_function ('starts at the lowest level... the output... and works upward toward the source') and practical_application (amp/speakers first, then back to source) describe output-to-source, while the definition and plain_english describe source-to-output. Rewrite the definition and plain_english to match the output-to-source direction used in purpose_function and practical_application (e.g., definition: 'Starting diagnosis at the output/lowest level of a signal path and working back toward the source, useful when the output or physical layer is suspect.'), or flip the other two fields instead — but all four must agree.

suggestions.issue: Redundant list item. The third bullet ('Forgetting that a wider apex angle raises the tension in each leg for the same suspended load.') simply restates the point already made in detail by the first bullet ('the wider the included angle, the higher the tension in each leg for the same suspended load...').
suggestions.suggestion: Delete the third bullet ('Forgetting that a wider apex angle raises the tension in each leg for the same suspended load.') since the first bullet already covers apex-angle/tension; this removes the duplication without losing content.

suggestions.issue: The last item ('a re-terminated connector with the conductors (not jacket) taking the strain') is a sentence fragment, not a statement of a mistake, and breaks the parallel verb-led structure of the other bullets. It leaves the mistake implicit.
suggestions.suggestion: Rewrite as an action, e.g., 'Re-terminating a connector so the conductors (not the jacket) take the strain, instead of using proper strain relief.'
